```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(scipen = 999)
#install.packages("meta")
#install.packages("metafor")
#install.packages("emmeans")
library(emmeans)
library(meta)
library(metafor)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(lme4)
```

## Overview

This script contains code to perform meta-analysis in the article. The cleaned data is provided in the GitHub repository.

## Load data

```{r}
df_roi_grand = read_excel("./Data/ROI_data_analysis.xlsx", 
    sheet = "Bivariate results")

# select relevant columns and subset for studies with bivariate analysis
df_roi = df_roi_grand %>% dplyr::select(c(1,3,7,9,11,13,14,39,41:43, 48,62:63, 70:72, 99:102)) %>%
  filter(`Bivariate done` == "Y")
# overall data (dataset to use for all race of respondents combined) 
df_roi_overall = df_roi_grand %>% dplyr::select(c(1,3,7,9,11,13,14,39,41:43, 48,62:63, 70:72, 95:98)) %>%
  filter(`Bivariate done` == "Y") %>%
  mutate(total_qs = `total #NR`+ `total #R`,
         sig_qs = round(`total #sig NR`+ `total #sig R`,0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(1:17,22:23)


## Subset data by race of respondents and whether the analysis involves YEAR
# for analysis involving YEAR 
df_roi_year = df_roi_overall[-c(1,2),]
# for all analysis not involving YEAR
df_roi_else = df_roi_overall[-27,]

# data set for Blacks
# no YEAR
df_roi_black = df_roi %>% filter(ROR_Black == "Yes")
# with YEAR
df_roi_black_year = df_roi_black[-c(1,2),]

# data set for Whites
# no YEAR
df_roi_white = df_roi %>% filter(ROR_White == "Yes")
# with YEAR
df_roi_white_else = df_roi_white[-16,]
```


## Phase 1: Meta-analysis by study-level predictors that do not vary within a study

These analyses fit the GLMM specified in the article (phase 1). The code enables analysis by Black and White respondent groups separately and also overall (Black, White, Hispanic respondents). 

### Analysis for overall sample (all race of respondents combined)

```{r overall_phase1}
meta_overall_else = metaprop(
  event = sig_qs,
  n = total_qs,
  studlab = `Author(s)`,
  data = df_roi_else,
  sm = "PLOGIT",
  method = "GLMM",
  common  = FALSE,
  random = TRUE,
  keepdata = TRUE
)
mods = names(df_roi_else)[c(3:5, 8:11)]
df_roi_else[mods] = lapply(df_roi_else[mods], factor)

subgroup_roi_else_overall = lapply(mods, function(v) {
  df_roi_else[[v]] = factor(df_roi_else[[v]])
  res = update(
    meta_overall_else,
    subgroup      = df_roi_else[[v]],
    print.subgroup.name = FALSE  
  )
  
  res
})
names(subgroup_roi_else_overall) = mods

## Analysis involving YEAR
meta_overall_year = metaprop(
  event = sig_qs,
  n = total_qs,
  studlab = `Author(s)`,
  data = df_roi_year,
  sm = "PLOGIT",
  method = "GLMM",
  common  = FALSE,
  random = TRUE,
  keepdata = TRUE
)
mods_y = names(df_roi_year)[2]
df_roi_year[mods_y] = lapply(df_roi_year[mods_y], factor)

subgroup_roi_year_overall = lapply(mods_y, function(v) {
  df_roi_year[[v]] = factor(df_roi_year[[v]])
  res = update(
    meta_overall_year,
    subgroup      = df_roi_year[[v]],
    print.subgroup.name = FALSE
  )
  
  res
})
names(subgroup_roi_year_overall) = mods_y

# Table 3 (panel 4-10) and Table S1, S2 in Appendix B created from the following results
print(subgroup_roi_else_overall) 
print(subgroup_roi_year_overall)
```

### Analysis for Black respondents

## Phase 2: Meta-regression for predictors that vary within a study

The code blocks below perform meta-regression analysis that fits a multilevel mixed-effects model with random intercepts for studies to assess associations between the reported proportion of items being statistically significant for ROI effect and predictors that vary within a study (phase 2).

### Analysis for race of respondents

```{r ror_phase2}
df_race = df_roi_grand %>% dplyr::select(c(1,14,64:65,99:104)) %>% filter(`Bivariate done` == "Y")
df_race_group = df_race[-27,] %>% dplyr::select(1, 5:10)
colnames(df_race_group) = c("Authors", "total_items_Black", "sig_items_Black", "total_items_White", "sig_items_White", "total_items_Hispanic", "sig_items_Hispanic")
df_race_long_mv = df_race_group %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      total_items_Black, sig_items_Black,
      total_items_White, sig_items_White,
      total_items_Hispanic, sig_items_Hispanic
    ),
    names_to = c(".value", "race"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(Black|White|Hispanic)$"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    race = factor(
      race,
      levels = c("Black", "White", "Hispanic")
    ),
    total_items = as.numeric(total_items),
    sig_items = as.numeric(sig_items)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(total_items),
    !is.na(sig_items),
    total_items > 0,
    sig_items >= 0,
    sig_items <= total_items,
    total_items == floor(total_items),
    sig_items == floor(sig_items)
  )
dat_race_es = escalc(
  measure = "PLO",
  xi = sig_items,
  ni = total_items,
  data = df_race_long_mv
)
fit_race_mv = rma.mv(
  yi,
  vi,
  mods = ~ race,
  random = ~ 1 | Authors,
  data = dat_race_es,
  method = "REML"
)

## Model results (tests in Table S1 and Table 3)
summary(fit_race_mv)

new_race = data.frame(
  race = factor(
    c("Black", "White", "Hispanic"),
    levels = levels(dat_race_es$race)
  )
)

X_race = model.matrix(
  ~ race,
  data = new_race
)

pred_race = predict(
  fit_race_mv,
  newmods = X_race[, -1, drop = FALSE],
  transf = transf.ilogit
)

results_race_mv = data.frame(
  race = new_race$race,
  pooled_proportion = pred_race$pred,
  ci_lower = pred_race$ci.lb,
  ci_upper = pred_race$ci.ub
)
## Pooled proportions in Table 3 panel 1
results_race_mv
```

### Analysis for overall sample (Nonracial vs. racial and Factual vs. attitudinal items)

```{r overall_phase2}

# 1. Nonracial vs. Racial Items
## Data preparation
df_overall = df_roi_grand %>% dplyr::select(1,13:14, 48,95:98) %>% filter(`Bivariate done` == "Y")
colnames(df_overall) = c("Authors", "multivariate_done", "bivariate_done", "quality_measure", "total_NR", "sig_NR", "total_R", "sig_R")
df_overall_long = df_overall %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_NR, sig_NR, total_R, sig_R),
    names_to = c(".value", "type"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(NR|R)$"
  ) %>%
  rename(total_questions = total,
         sig_questions = sig) %>%
  # Remove rows where both total and sig are missing/NA
  filter(!is.na(total_questions) & !is.na(sig_questions)) %>%
  # Keep only rows where total > 0 (i.e., study reported this type)
  filter(total_questions > 0)

df_overall.long = escalc(
  measure = "PLO",           # Proportions with logit transformation
  xi = sig_questions,        
  ni = total_questions,      
  data = df_overall_long
)
## Setting nonracial as the reference level
df_overall.long$type = relevel(
  factor(df_overall.long$type),
  ref = "nonracial"
)

## Model fitting
res_overall = rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  mods = ~ type,
  random = ~ 1 | Authors,    # Random effect for study (Authors)
  data = df_overall.long,
  method = "REML"
)
## Model results (Table 3 (panel 2), S1 and S3 in Appendix B)
print(res_overall)

## Get pooled estimates
overall_nr = predict(res_overall, newmods = 0, transf = transf.ilogit)
overall_r = predict(res_overall, newmods = 1, transf = transf.ilogit)

results_table_overall = data.frame(
  Group = c("Overall", "Overall"),
  Type = c("Nonracial", "Racial"),
  Pooled_Proportion = c(round(overall_nr$pred,2), round(overall_r$pred,2)),
  CI_Lower = c(round(overall_nr$ci.lb,2), round(overall_r$ci.lb,2)),
  CI_Upper = c(round(overall_nr$ci.ub,2), round(overall_r$ci.ub,2))
)

## 2. Factual vs. Attitudinal Items

df_attfact = df_roi_grand %>% dplyr::select(c(1,3,7,9,11,13,14,39,41:43, 48,62:63, 70:72, 105:120)) %>% filter(`Bivariate done` == "Y")
df_attfact_overall = df_attfact %>% dplyr::select(1, 30:33)
colnames(df_attfact_overall) = c("Authors", "total_attitude", "sig_attitude", "total_fact", "sig_fact")
df_attfact_overall_long = df_attfact_overall %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_attitude, sig_attitude, total_fact, sig_fact),
    names_to = c(".value", "type"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(attitude|fact)$"
  ) %>%
  rename(total_questions = total,
         sig_questions = sig) %>%
  # Remove rows where both total and sig are missing/NA
  filter(!is.na(total_questions) & !is.na(sig_questions)) %>%
  # Keep only rows where total > 0 (i.e., study reported this type)
  filter(total_questions > 0)

df_attfact_overall_long = escalc(
  measure = "PLO",           # Proportions with logit transformation
  xi = sig_questions,        
  ni = total_questions,     
  data = df_attfact_overall_long
)
## setting factual as reference level
df_attfact_overall_long$type = relevel(
  factor(df_attfact_overall_long$type),
  ref = "fact"
)

res_attfact_overall = rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  mods = ~ type,
  random = ~ 1 | Authors,    # Random effect for study (Authors)
  data = df_attfact_overall_long,
  method = "REML"
)
## Model results (Table 3 (panel 3), S1 and S3 in Appendix B)
print(res_attfact_overall)
## Get pooled estimates
overall_fact = predict(res_attfact_overall, newmods = 0, transf = transf.ilogit)
overall_attitude = predict(res_attfact_overall, newmods = 1, transf = transf.ilogit)

attfact_results_table_overall = data.frame(
  Group = c("Overall", "Overall"),
  Type = c("Attitude", "Fact"),
  Pooled_Proportion = c(round(overall_attitude$pred,2), round(overall_fact$pred,2)),
  CI_Lower = c(round(overall_attitude$ci.lb,2), round(overall_fact$ci.lb,2)),
  CI_Upper = c(round(overall_attitude$ci.ub,2), round(overall_fact$ci.ub,2))
)
```
